The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Irregular dark brown/black blotchy spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Leaf rolling/curling lengthwise
- Varying spot sizes, some confluent dark patches
- Green background tissue still visible

Key candidates: **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (dark necrotic spots + leaf distortion), **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato** (dark spots), or **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**. The combination of irregular dark blotches AND leaf curling/distortion points strongly toward TSWV. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The TSWV reference shows systemic wilting at a whole-plant level, but TSWV is known to also manifest as dark necrotic spots with leaf distortion at earlier stages. The test image shows:
- Prominent leaf rolling/curling (distortion)
- Irregular dark brown-black blotchy necrotic lesions
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight), no gray centers (rules out Septoria), no powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)

The irregular dark necrotic spots combined with significant leaf distortion/curling is characteristic of **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (caused by thrips-transmitted tospovirus), which produces bronze-brown necrotic spots and leaf rolling as hallmark symptoms.
